meta.guide:
Choosing steel MIG wire

PLATINUM XT6 (ER70S-6)

PLATINUM XT6 is a premium S6 grade, copper-coated low carbon steel MIG wire. It is layer wound and made under strict quality control for reliable feeding, with low spatter and low fume. It suits a wide range of mild and mid-strength low carbon steels and galvanised steel, and welds in all positions including vertical down. Use it with argon or CO2 based gas mixtures.

ER70S-6 mini-spools

The ER70S-6 mini-spools are 0.9kg spools on a D100 (100mm) hub, for machines that take 1kg spools. They give low spatter, good edge wetting and weld shape on mild and mid-strength steels, with argon mixed gas or CO2.

Matching wire to your welder

Check which spool sizes your machine takes. The FORCE 132MST takes 1kg (D100mm) spools only. The FORCE 180MST takes 1kg or 5kg spools, and the FORCE 200MST takes 5kg or 15kg spools. Solid steel wire needs shielding gas. If you are welding outdoors without gas, see the gasless wire range.

meta.guide:
How to choose a Weldclass MIG welder

Start with your power supply

Six models are fitted with a 10A plug: the FORCE 132MST, FORCE 160MST, FORCE 180MST and the FURY 165, 185 and 205 MPST Pulse. The FORCE 200MST, 205MST, 255MST, ULTRA 250MST and FORCE 290MST come with a 15A plug. The FORCE 350MST has a 3-phase 32A plug.

Match output and duty cycle to the work

Rated duty cycle tells you how long a machine runs at full output. The 180MST gives 180A @ 10%, while the 205MST gives 200A @ 30% and the 255MST 250A @ 35%. For all-day production, the 290MST (290A @ 55%), 350MST (350A @ 60%) and 395MST Pulse (400A @ 60%) take wires up to 1.2mm and can run with a separate wire feeder.

Pulse, synergic or manual

The FURY MPST machines offer pulse mode in MIG, Stick and TIG, which gives lower spatter and less heat input on aluminium, stainless and mild steel. Synergic MIG is available on the 132MST, the FURY range, the ULTRA 250MST and the FORCE 205MST and larger FORCE models. With synergic, you set the wire and material thickness and the machine sets the parameters.

Spool size and aluminium

The 132MST takes 1kg spools only. The 200MST, 255MST, ULTRA 250MST, 290MST, 350MST and 395MST take 5kg or 15kg spools. Most models are spool gun ready for aluminium wire.

meta.intro: ALLCLEAR fume control by Weldclass covers on-torch extractors, mobile extraction units with 3m arms, downdraft and fixture-point tables, wall-mounted fans and the PD30 wearable fume monitor. Single-phase and 3-phase options are available, and ALLCLEAR on-torch, mobile and TA-series table units carry a 7-year warranty offer when registered online within 30 days of purchase.
meta.guide:
How to choose a fume extractor

On-torch extractors

On-torch units capture fume at the gun and follow the weld. They are for gas MIG, gasless and flux-core welding. The ALLCLEAR MT31 runs on 230V 10A with 200m3/hr max airflow for light-to-medium industrial use. The ALLCLEAR MT84 runs on 230V 15A with dual motors, 380m3/hr and a HEPA H13 filter, for high-volume, frequent use.

Mobile extractors

Mobile units suit MIG, flux-core, TIG, plasma cutting, grinding and arc gouging. The MA100 and MA300 AUTO run on 230V 10A with one 3m arm. The MA350 STD and MA350 AUTO run on 415V with twin 3m arms. For high-fume work such as some flux-core wires, Weldclass recommends the AUTO models, which clean the filter with compressed air.

Downdraft tables

The TA100 (230V) suits welding and light grinding. The TA400, TA500 and FP Series are 415V tables for heavier welding and grinding.

Monitoring and limits

The PD30 is a wearable monitor that shows TWA fume readings on the device to support compliance with Australian legislation. None of these extractors are suitable for fume containing aluminium dust, oil mist, gases or water vapour. The FA25 wall fan has no filter and needs a suitable filtration system for welding fume.

faq.q: Which ALLCLEAR fume extractor suits high-fume flux-cored welding?
faq.a: For high-fume applications such as some flux-core wires, Weldclass recommends the ALLCLEAR MA300 AUTO or MA350 AUTO Mobile Welding Fume Extractor. Both clean their cartridge filters automatically with compressed air, which keeps suction consistent. The MA300 AUTO runs on 230V 10A and the MA350 AUTO runs on 415V 3-phase.

faq.q: Can ALLCLEAR fume extractors be used for aluminium?
faq.a: ALLCLEAR extractors and downdraft tables are not suitable for fumes containing aluminium dust, oil mist, gases or water vapour. Aluminium dust, including grinding dust, can be explosive when airborne. Weldclass notes aluminium welding fume itself is safe to extract, but most on-torch aluminium applications carry a high risk of dust being present.

faq.q: What does the ALLCLEAR PD30 fume monitor measure?
faq.a: The ALLCLEAR PD30 Welding Fume Monitor is worn by the welder and detects particles from 0.3 to 10 microns. It shows a real-time TWA (time-weighted average) reading on the device, warns on inhalable and respirable TWA8H and STEL, and runs 12+ hours at a 1-second sample rate.

faq.q: Which ALLCLEAR extractors run on single-phase power?
faq.a: The ALLCLEAR MT31 on-torch extractor, MA100 and MA300 AUTO mobile extractors, TA100 downdraft table and FA25 wall fan run on single-phase 230V 10A. The ALLCLEAR MT84 on-torch extractor needs 230V 15A. The MA350 models, TA400, TA500 and FP Series need 415V 3-phase.

faq.q: Does the ALLCLEAR FA25 wall fan filter welding fume?
faq.a: No. The ALLCLEAR FA25 is an extraction fan only, with no filter. It suits mild, non-toxic airborne contaminants as supplied. For welding and grinding fumes it must be used with a suitable filtration system, often a ducted system to a central extraction or filter unit.

meta.guide:
Choosing gasless MIG wire

Why E71T-11 matters

All three Weldclass gasless wires are E71T-11 classification (AWS A5.20), which suits multi-pass welding. Weldclass points out that many mini-spools on the market are E71T-GS grade, which is for single-pass welding only.

PLATINUM GL-11

PLATINUM GL-11 is described by Weldclass as Australia's number one gasless MIG wire. It has a smooth arc, low spatter, low fume and easy de-slagging. It handles moderately rusty, dirty or painted steel. It comes on vacuum foil-sealed spools for storage life, in 0.8mm, 0.9mm, 1.2mm and 1.6mm, on 4.5kg and 15kg spools.

PROMAX T11

PROMAX T11 is the value option. It is also E71T-11, layer wound, vacuum foil-sealed and rated for single and multi-pass welds in all positions on mild and galvanised steel. It also carries AS/NZS ISO 17632-B-T49ZT11-1NA classification.

Mini-spools

The gasless mini-spools are 0.9kg on a 100mm spool, for small jobs and spool guns. They suit outdoor and onsite work and welding in windy conditions, and give a smooth arc with minimal spatter on mild and galvanised steel.

meta.intro: Weldclass stick and TIG welders cover portable repair work through to AC/DC TIG on aluminium. The FORCE 135ST weighs 2.3kg and runs 3.2mm electrodes from a 10A plug, the FORCE 180ST delivers 180A and runs electrodes up to 4.0mm, and the FORCE 201T AC/DC Pulse delivers 200A @ 30% on AC TIG.
meta.guide:
How to choose a stick or TIG welder

Electrode size and power supply

The FORCE 135ST is fitted with a 10A 240V plug and runs electrodes up to 3.2mm, with 140A @ 20% duty cycle. The FORCE 180ST moves up to a 15A plug, 180A @ 18% and electrodes up to 4.0mm. If you only have a 10A outlet, the 135ST is the one to pick.

DC lift-arc TIG or AC/DC TIG

The 135ST and 180ST both do DC lift-arc TIG for steel and stainless. A TIG torch (17FV 4m) and gas regulator are optional extras. For aluminium you need AC TIG, which means the FORCE 201T AC/DC Pulse. It comes with an 8m #26 flexi TIG torch with remote current control, gas regulator, tungstens and a parts kit, and adds HF or lift-arc ignition, pulse adjustment from 0.2 to 200Hz, AC balance and slope controls. Foot controllers are available separately.

Generators and site work

All three are generator compatible. The 135ST needs a minimum 7kVA (8kVA ideal), and the 180ST and 201T need a minimum 8kVA (10kVA or more ideal). The 135ST and 180ST have adjustable hot start and arc force, plus an optional VRD that an authorised agent or distributor can activate.

faq.q: Can I TIG weld aluminium with the FORCE 135ST or FORCE 180ST?
faq.a: No. The FORCE 135ST and FORCE 180ST are DC lift-arc TIG machines, suited to steel and stainless. TIG welding aluminium needs AC/DC TIG capability, which in the Weldclass range is the FORCE 201T AC/DC Pulse, rated at 200A @ 30% duty cycle in AC TIG.

faq.q: Which Weldclass stick welder runs on a 10A power point?
faq.a: The FORCE 135ST Stick/TIG Welder is fitted with a 10A 240V plug and runs electrodes up to 3.2mm, with 140A @ 20% duty cycle. It weighs 2.3kg. The FORCE 180ST and FORCE 201T are fitted with 15A plugs.

faq.q: Is a TIG torch included with the FORCE 135ST and 180ST?
faq.a: No. The FORCE 135ST and FORCE 180ST come with earth and stick leads and a shoulder strap. The TIG Torch 17FV 4m (WC-00992) and gas regulator (4-AR1) are optional accessories. The FORCE 201T AC/DC Pulse includes an 8m #26 TIG torch and a gas regulator.

faq.q: What size generator do I need for a Weldclass stick welder?
faq.a: The FORCE 135ST needs a generator of at least 7kVA, with 8kVA ideal. The FORCE 180ST and FORCE 201T AC/DC Pulse need at least 8kVA, with 10kVA or more ideal.

meta.meta_desc: The Weldclass FORCE 45P plasma cutter cleanly cuts 20mm mild steel and severs 25mm, runs from a 15A 240V plug, weighs 8kg and has PFC. RRP $1,690.
meta.intro: The Weldclass FORCE 45P is a single-phase plasma cutter rated at 40A @ 45% duty cycle. It cleanly cuts mild steel up to 20mm and severs up to 25mm, weighs 8kg and runs from a 15A 240V plug. RRP is $1,690 incl. GST through Weldclass distributors.
meta.guide:
Choosing a plasma cutter

Cut capacity

Plasma cutters are rated two ways. Clean cut is the thickness you can cut with a usable edge, and severance is the most the machine will part. The FORCE 45P clean cuts up to 20mm mild steel, 18mm stainless and 14mm aluminium, and severs up to 25mm mild steel, 22mm stainless and 20mm aluminium.

Power supply, leads and generators

The 45P is fitted with a 15A 240V plug. Power Factor Correction (PFC) reduces power draw and lifts duty cycle, so it can run on extension leads up to 100m. On generator power it needs a minimum 8kVA, with 10kVA or more ideal.

Air supply

You need a compressor with at least 120L/min (4.5cfm) free air delivery. An air regulator with filter and Nitto-style fitting is included, and Weldclass recommends adding the PLATINUM Z-20 air filter for better cutting and longer parts life.

Other features

  • Pilot arc ignition, non-HF, to avoid EMF interference
  • Perforated plate and expanded mesh cutting mode
  • Euro-connection torch, 6m, with parts kit
  • 4m earth lead, 3m power input lead, shoulder strap and cable strap included

The FORCE 45P carries a 7-year warranty offer, which requires online registration within 30 days of purchase. Find a stockist through Where to buy.

faq.q: How thick can the FORCE 45P plasma cutter cut?
faq.a: The FORCE 45P Plasma Cutter clean cuts mild steel up to 20mm, stainless steel up to 18mm and aluminium up to 14mm. Its severance capacity is 25mm mild steel, 22mm stainless steel and 20mm aluminium, at 40A @ 45% duty cycle.

faq.q: What size air compressor does the FORCE 45P need?
faq.a: The FORCE 45P Plasma Cutter needs a compressor that delivers at least 120L/min (4.5cfm) free air delivery. An air regulator with filter and Nitto-style fitting is supplied, and Weldclass recommends the PLATINUM Z-20 air filter for optimum cutting and longer parts life.

faq.q: Can I run the FORCE 45P on a generator?
faq.a: Yes. The FORCE 45P Plasma Cutter is generator friendly, needing a minimum 8kVA generator, with 10kVA or more ideal. Its Power Factor Correction (PFC) also allows use on extension leads up to 100m.

faq.q: What plug does the FORCE 45P use?
faq.a: The FORCE 45P Plasma Cutter is fitted with a 15A 240V plug and runs on single-phase power. It weighs 8kg and comes with a 3m power input lead, 6m plasma torch and 4m earth lead.

meta.meta_desc: Weldclass steel welding rods: PLATINUM 12V and PROMAX GP E6013 general purpose electrodes, and PLATINUM 16XT E7016 low hydrogen for high-strength steel.
meta.intro: Weldclass stocks two general purpose E6013 electrodes for mild and galvanised steel, PLATINUM 12V and PROMAX GP, plus the PLATINUM 16XT E7016 low hydrogen electrode for high-strength steel and heavily loaded joints. All three are all-positional, and both E6013 rods weld vertical down.
meta.guide:
Choosing a steel electrode

General purpose (E6013)

For fabrication, repair, fencing and light structural work on mild, galvanised, plate, sheet and RHS steel, use a general purpose rod. PLATINUM 12V is the Weldclass best seller, with a smooth arc, low spatter and self-detaching slag. It comes in 2.0mm, 2.6mm (2.5mm) and 3.2mm. PROMAX GP is the same E6013 classification in a 1kg re-usable pack, in 2.0mm, 2.6mm and 3.2mm. Weldclass recommends PLATINUM 12V when you want a more forceful arc or use larger volumes.

Low hydrogen (E7016)

PLATINUM 16XT is a hydrogen-controlled electrode for mild and high-strength carbon-manganese steels up to 510MPa. Use it where the joint needs more strength than a GP rod: highly restrained joints, parts under higher load, mining maintenance, structural and site work, pipe, boilers and pressure vessels, and as a buffer layer before hard facing. It comes in foil-sealed 2kg vacuum packs to keep moisture out, in 2.5mm, 3.2mm and 4.0mm. It is all-positional except vertical down.

Check your machine's OCV

Minimum recommended open circuit voltage is 40V for PLATINUM 12V and 45V for PROMAX GP.

faq.q: What is the difference between PLATINUM 12V and PLATINUM 16XT electrodes?
faq.a: PLATINUM 12V is an E6013 general purpose electrode for mild and galvanised steel, all-positional including vertical down. PLATINUM 16XT is an E7016 H8 low hydrogen electrode for mild and high-strength steels up to 510MPa, used where joints need higher strength. It is all-positional except vertical down.

faq.q: How many PLATINUM 12V rods are in a kilogram?
faq.a: PLATINUM 12V 2.6mm electrodes run approximately 50 rods per kg, or 125 rods per 2.5kg packet. The 3.2mm size runs approximately 33 rods per kg, or 83 rods per 2.5kg packet.

faq.q: Which Weldclass electrode should I use on galvanised steel?
faq.a: Both general purpose E6013 electrodes, PLATINUM 12V and PROMAX GP, are rated for mild and galvanised steel, including plate, sheet and tubular/RHS. Both tolerate dirty or rusty steel and poor fit-up, and weld in all positions including vertical down.

faq.q: Why does PLATINUM 16XT come in vacuum-sealed packs?
faq.a: PLATINUM 16XT is a low hydrogen electrode. Moisture absorbed from the air raises hydrogen levels in the electrode, which compromises weld strength and can affect the arc. The foil-sealed 2kg vacuum packs keep moisture out up to the point of use and reduce waste.
